inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E for the enlarged (post-injection) group: H1 2026 actual RMB189,338m (interim report p.111) plus an H2 estimate of ~RMB180,700m. Management's adjusted FY2026 revenue target is RMB360,000m (Q1 2026 report, 'Adjusted business targets'); H1 delivered 52.6% of it and management guided H2 coal prices 'trending moderately higher', so the anchor sits between the target and a straight 2x H1 run-rate (RMB378.7bn). The pre-injection FY2025 revenue of RMB294,916m is NOT the base: the 12-company injection added ~27% to revenue (H1 2025 restated RMB175,423m vs RMB138,109m as originally reported).
inputs.share_count_basis: 21,689m ordinary shares (A + H) in issue at 30 June 2026 after the 1,363m consideration shares to China Energy (Mar-2026) and the ~457m supporting-fund A-share placement (Apr-2026); interim report balance sheet note 26. No options, convertibles or share schemes: basic = diluted (EPS note 12). Held flat.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026. total_debt = current borrowings 82,705 + non-current borrowings 74,923 + lease liabilities 1,213 (181 current + 1,032 non-current). cash = cash and cash equivalents 51,673 + time deposits with original maturity over three months 65,722 + structured deposits held at FVTPL (current) 6,701. Excluded from cash: restricted bank deposits 18,197 (mine geological environment restoration fund) which is treated as matching the 14,982 accrued reclamation obligation, both left out of the bridge. RMB70,200m of the group's deposits sit with China Energy Finance Co. (60% parent-owned) under a RMB75bn cap -- counted as cash here but a related-party concentration the reader should know about. The RMB38,116m of deferred mining-rights payables (long-term liabilities 28,188 + current portion 9,928) is debt-like and is deducted in equity_bridge rather than in net_debt so the metrics-table total_debt still reconciles.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026E consolidated FCF (OCF less capex, pre-NCI) for the enlarged group: H1 2026 actual 54,664 - 27,367 = 27,297 (interim cash flow statement) plus an H2 estimate of ~24,700, which assumes H2 OCF near H1 and H2 cash capex of ~RMB30bn (the adjusted FY2026 capex plan is RMB55,987m excluding mining rights, of which RMB23,290m was completed on an accrual basis in H1). The last audited pre-injection actual (FY2025) was reported FCF 28,385 / owner FCF 26,098 on the smaller entity and is not a usable base.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment: Chinese central SOE with no equity-compensation scheme; StockBasedComp and EquityAwardTaxes are nil in every period FY2017-H1 2026 (Metrics CSV). House and street bases coincide; band_position collapses to null.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026E: H1 2026 interest income RMB1,091m (income statement) annualised; stripped from owner FCF because the ~RMB124bn cash and deposits pile is added back in the bridge. FY2025 actual was 2,287.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1722, Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-09. Statements are in RMB (ISO CNY); the H-share quotes in HKD. Per-share values are computed in CNY and multiplied by 1.1722 for the HKD headline. Dual-listing check: the A-share (601088.SS) closed at CNY48.40 on 2026-10-09 = HKD56.7 at this rate against the H-share's HKD44.22 -- a 28% A/H premium, which is normal for Shenhua (A shares have traded at a persistent premium), so the rate and direction are confirmed but there is no parity tie; this valuation is of the H-share.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10y CGB ~1.8% + beta 0.95 x China equity risk premium ~6.5% (which already embeds country risk) = cost of equity ~8.0%; after-tax cost of debt ~2.3% (SOE bank borrowing ~3% x (1-0.21)); weights ~90/10 at market value (CNY ~820bn market cap vs RMB159bn gross debt) -> 7.4%, rounded to 7.5%. No cyclicality, carbon-transition or SOE-governance premium is stacked on top: those risks are charged once, in the scenario paths and the 25% bear weight. Same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities RMB1,213m are inside total_debt; lease principal (H1 2026: 377) is NOT deducted from the flows; ongoing lease-asset renewal is covered by the capex path (the 'increase in right-of-use assets' investing line, 2,212 in H1, is land-use rights and is treated as part of capex intensity). Leases are immaterial (0.1% of assets) so the choice barely moves the value, but it is stated so it cannot be charged twice later.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: non-controlling interests (RMB99,608m at book; 18.4% of H1 2026 profit, 7,010 of 38,064) are folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax-plus-NCI leakage on EBIT of 35.5% = 1 - (1 - 0.207 effective tax) x (1 - 0.184 NCI share). Calibration: H1 2026 EBIT (company-definition EBITDA 65,177 less D&A 17,171 = 48,006) x (1 - 0.355) = 31,060 vs reported attributable profit 31,054. NCI is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge. The book-value alternative (tax at 20.7%, deduct 99.6bn NCI) would be ~RMB2.6/share (~7%) higher because the NCI subsidiaries earn ~14% on book; the leakage route is the conservative and economically correct one.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (owner_fcf_dcf_component), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the adaptations file applied (CNY-built WACC, HKD quote, lease treatment A, NCI-in-flows, matching-asset rule, SBC-zero). Not a bank/REIT/LIC. Mid-cycle normalisation is applied through the EBITDA-margin paths rather than a reset of the base year: the FY2017-FY2025 pre-injection margin range was 30.1% (FY2021, purchased-coal surge) to 40.9% (FY2017), with FY2020 -- the coal-price trough -- at 34.3%; the enlarged group printed 34.4% in H1 2026 (company-definition EBITDA 65,177: PBT 48,028 + net finance costs 1,632 + D&A 17,171 - associates 1,654). Vertical integration (captive power and rail earn more when coal is cheap) is why the margin is so stable through the cycle; the base case fades it to 33% for the lower-margin injected power/chemical assets and declining coal-plant utilisation hours. STRUCTURAL BREAK: the Jan-Mar 2026 common-control injection of 12 companies (RMB133.6bn consideration; shares 19,869m -> 21,689m; gearing 23% -> 40%; installed capacity 52.7GW -> 70.6GW) makes every pre-2026 per-share, leverage and absolute-flow series non-comparable with the current entity, so the valuation is built on the FY2026E enlarged base and the historical CAGR block is a shape reference only. MATCHING-ASSET RULE: share of results of associates (H1 2026: 1,654; ~RMB3.5-4.5bn/yr) and interest income are excluded from the flows, so interests in associates (83,198, book) and the cash pile are added in the bridge; FVOCI equity instruments (7,211) are added because their dividend income is outside EBITDA. YEAR-1 FCF vs last_fcf: last_fcf (49,800) is a consolidated pre-NCI figure per the contract identity; the component build charges the NCI's ~RMB13-14bn/yr share through the 35.5% leakage rate, so modelled year-1 owner FCF (~RMB38-39bn) sits deliberately below last_fcf. Capex: the adjusted FY2026 plan is RMB56.0bn (15.1% of base revenue) against D&A of ~RMB33-34bn; the base case assumes the mine-replacement and power build-out cycle fades capex intensity to 11.5% of revenue by year 8, still above the ~9.5% D&A run-rate. Working capital: receivables + inventory (44.6bn) < payables + contract liabilities (62.0bn), so growth releases a little cash; wc_capture is held at 0 as the conservative round-off. Terminal cap 12x FCF in every scenario (cyclical, carbon-exposed; the cap binds in base and bull) -- a buyer of a coal major does not pay the Gordon multiple.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 2.5% diverges by more than 30% from revenue (4.8%) and EPS (8.6%) 5yr CAGRs; all three are endpoint-sensitive because FY2020 was the coal-price trough and FY2022 the peak. The 3yr CAGRs are all negative for the same reason (FY2022 peak start point). Equity CAGR is depressed by the ~75-80% dividend payout, not by weak returns.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs are on the pre-injection entity (FY2020/FY2022 -> FY2025, Metrics CSV) and are a shape reference only: the Jan-Mar 2026 asset injection breaks the series. Owner-FCF CAGRs (reported FCF less interest income; SBC is nil) are slightly below reported-FCF CAGRs only because interest income fell with the cash balance. FCF CAGRs are dominated by the capex ramp (FY2021 23.2bn -> FY2025 46.7bn), not by operating decline: OCF fell 21% over FY2020-25 while capex more than doubled.

base.narrative: Coal prices hold near the government-guided band (RMB 650-800/t long-term contract reference); volumes from the enlarged mine portfolio are flat-to-slightly-up as new mines (Xinjie, Tarangaole, Boligou, Hongshaquan No.2) replace depletion; power generation grows with capacity but utilisation hours keep falling; transport and chemicals add low-single-digit growth. Nominal revenue growth fades from 3% to 1% and terminal growth is 1%, below CNY inflation, to reflect coal's secular decline. EBITDA margin fades from 34% to 33% as the injected power/chemical assets dilute the coal mix. Capex intensity retreats from the current 15% build-out to 11.5% by year 8 (still above D&A). Combined tax+NCI leakage flat at 35.5%.

bull.narrative: Coal supply stays tight (safety-driven output curbs, slower approvals) and prices firm toward the JPMorgan RMB830/t 2026 view; the injected power and chemical assets integrate cleanly and lift segment margins; coal-to-olefins upgrading and the 2,712MW new-energy portfolio add growth; capex falls back toward 10% of revenue as the current mine/power build-out completes, releasing cash to the ~75-80% payout. Margin ~35% sustained, growth 6% fading to 2%, terminal growth 2%.

bear.narrative: Decarbonisation bites early: renewables (already >60% of national capacity) keep eroding coal-plant utilisation hours, industrial coal demand (steel, cement) contracts, and coal prices retrace to 2020-trough levels (~RMB550/t) as supply loosens. Revenue falls ~10% over four years then flatlines in nominal terms; EBITDA margin compresses below the 9-year historical floor to 30.5% because the integration hedge only partly offsets a volume-and-price decline. Capex stays policy-driven (energy-security mandates, the parent's project pipeline) and does not retreat below 13.5% of revenue; D&A rises on the enlarged asset base. Terminal growth 0%. Governance axis: further related-party injections or parent-priced coal contracts are not modelled explicitly but are why the bear weight is above the house default.

scenario_narratives.base: Coal-price band holds; enlarged group earns ~33-34% EBITDA margins; nominal growth 3% fading to 1%; capex intensity normalises from 15% to 11.5% of revenue over eight years; terminal growth 1%, terminal multiple capped at 12x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Tight coal market and clean integration of the injected assets: ~35% margins, 6% growth fading to 2%, capex back to 10% of revenue, 2% terminal growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: Early decarbonisation and a coal-price retrace to trough levels: revenue -10% over four years then flat, margin 30.5%, capex stuck at 13.5-15.5% of revenue, 0% terminal growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: thermal coal faces a multi-decade structural demand decline in China, the enlarged group is more leveraged (gearing 40%) and more power-heavy than the entity whose history we have, and the controlling shareholder is both the largest customer (~30% of coal volume) and the counterparty on every asset injection -- a single-counterparty governance dependency the method says warrants a heavier bear. Bull held at 25%, not 35%, because it needs three independent things to go right at once: coal prices firm, capex retreats, and no further dilutive or cash-draining related-party transactions. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A vertically integrated coal-power-rail conglomerate is valued as the owner-FCF stream it actually produces after real capex and after the minority partners' share, not on the ~79% dividend payout the market anchors to. The structural question is whether the current RMB56bn/yr capital programme is mine replacement (value-preserving) or policy-driven expansion (value-dilutive); the base case assumes it fades, the bear assumes it does not. The terminal value is capped at 12x FCF because the market will not pay a Gordon multiple for a coal major, and that cap -- not the WACC -- is what sets the headline in base and bull.
key_risks_to_valuation: Coal price: each RMB50/t move on ~620Mt of sales is roughly RMB30bn of revenue and, with integration offsets, perhaps RMB10-15bn of EBITDA -- the dominant swing factor the three scenarios bracket
Capex intensity: if the RMB56bn/yr programme does not fade toward D&A, base owner FCF never reaches the modelled year-10 level; every 1pp of revenue in perpetual capex is ~RMB4bn/yr of FCF

Related-party governance: ~30% of coal sales to the parent, RMB70bn of deposits at the parent's Finance Company, and a demonstrated pattern of share-funded asset injections at parent-set prices (the March 2026 consideration shares were issued at RMB29.40 vs an A-share price of ~RMB43-48)

NCI leakage: 18% of profit accrues to minority partners in subsidiaries; charged at 35.5% combined leakage, which ties to H1 2026 attributable profit but assumes the NCI share does not rise with the injected assets

Decarbonisation policy: coal-plant utilisation hours are falling every year; the base case's 33% margin and 1% terminal growth assume the decline is gradual and offset by chemicals, transport and new energy
Currency: the valuation is in CNY converted at 1.1722; a 5% CNY depreciation against HKD lowers the HKD headline ~5% with no change in the business
